stories.headline: Kamara's Knee Buckles in Dallas, and Travis Etienne Just Inherited the Whole Bayou
stories.read: Alvin Kamara got tangled up in a pile at that joint practice with the Cowboys and come out of it with a sprained MCL, and the wire says he's laid up at least a month. New Orleans opens in Detroit on September 13th, pardner, so do the arithmetic: he ain't ridin' Week 1, and maybe not Week 4 neither. That leaves Travis Etienne, who the Saints just backed a twelve-million-a-year wagon up to this spring, takin' every first-team rein in camp. Half the fellas in your outfit still got Kamara penciled where he sat in July. Go stake Etienne while he's cheap gold and let 'em pay retail for a man in a knee brace.

stories.headline: Jayden Higgins Goes Down for the Year, and Houston's Pecking Order Gets Redrawn
stories.read: Rough news out of the Raiders joint practice: Texans second-year man Jayden Higgins planted funny runnin' a route in the money patch and tore his ACL. Season's over before it started, and that's a 6-foot-4 target gone out of C.J. Stroud's huntin' ground. Now the saloon will tell you Nico Collins just got rich off it, and he does pick up a bigger cut of the throws, but hold up: with Higgins in the wagon, defenses can roll coverage at Collins and dare the other fellas to beat 'em. The real strike is Xavier Hutchinson, sittin' out there like free land at the tail end of every board. Stake that claim before somebody else reads the injury report.

stories.headline: Shedeur Sanders Got His Last Shot Under the Lights, and Cleveland Names Its Man This Week
stories.read: Saturday night the Bills took Cleveland behind the woodshed 31-7, but Shedeur Sanders went nine-for-eleven with a touchdown behind a second-string line, which is about all a fella can do standin' in that mess. The Browns brass says they're namin' a regular-season starter early this week, so you'll know before you sit down for your land grab. Here's the play, and listen close: don't chase Sanders himself, chase what falls out of the decision. If the young fella wins it, Cleveland's pass-catchers get a livelier trigger and the saloon hasn't moved their price yet. Keep one eye on the wire Monday and be first to that creek.
